title: This Waterfall In Antarctica Looks Like It's Bleeding
description:
Bright red water pours out of solid white ice in Antarctica -- and it stumped scientists for almost a century. The real explanation involves ancient trapped seawater and an ecosystem that's been sealed off from the world for millions of years.

#shorts #sciencefacts #antarctica #didyouknow

scenes.text: There's a waterfall in Antarctica that looks like it's bleeding -- bright red water pouring out of solid white ice. It's real, and it's not blood.
It was first found in 1911 by geologist Thomas Griffith Taylor, who assumed the color came from red algae. He was wrong, and nobody actually figured out why for almost a hundred years.

The real cause is iron. A hidden reservoir of super salty water, trapped beneath the glacier, is rich in dissolved iron -- and when it finally reaches the surface and touches oxygen, it rusts almost instantly, turning blood red.
That water has been sealed under the ice for an extraordinarily long time -- some estimates put it at close to two million years, cut off completely from sunlight and the open air.

And it's not empty down there. Scientists have found an entire ecosystem of microbes living in that trapped water, surviving in total darkness with zero oxygen by feeding on the iron and sulfur itself.
In 2017, researchers finally mapped how the water actually travels up through the glacier. But one thing is still a genuine mystery -- nobody knows what triggers it to flow when it does.
Would you have guessed that red water was actually rust, not blood?
